deadline.value: Funded projects set their own deadlines, which may be earlier than the College's final deadlines. Final deadlines for overseas fee status: Feb 2027 entry Oct 1, 2026 (passed); June 2027 entry Feb 1, 2027. The October 2027 date is not yet listed (October 2026 entry closed June 1, 2026 for overseas applicants). Most students start in October.
deadline.quote: Some projects and funding opportunities may have earlier deadlines than the listed college deadlines listed below, so please check carefully. | February 2027 entry – 1 October 2026 for Overseas fee status and 20 November 2026 for Home fee status | June 2027 entry – 1 February 2027 for Overseas fee status and 11 April 2027 for Home fee status | October 2026 entry – 1 June 2026 for Overseas fee status and 25 August 2026 for Home fee status

also.quote: Please note the application deadlines on each funded project advert, as these may vary.
However, there are application deadlines for funded and self-funded PhDs starting in October, February and June, although most students are recruited for an October entry.

toefl_min.value: English Band D applies to NMES (the faculty that includes Physics) research degrees. TOEFL iBT tests before Jan 21, 2026: 92 overall with at least 23 in writing and 20 in each other skill; tests from Jan 21, 2026: 4.5 overall with at least 4 in each skill. IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with at least 6.0 in each skill. Tests must be within 2 years of the start date.
toefl_min.quote: Faculty of Natural, Mathematical & Engineering Sciences (PGR only) | Tests taken before 21 January 2026: | 92 overall with a minimum of 23 in writing and 20 in each of the other skills | Tests taken from 21 January 2026: | 4.5 overall with a minimum of 4 in each skill | 6.5 overall with a minimum of 6.0 in each skill

english_waiver.value: Exemption needs an undergraduate degree (at least 3 years), a taught postgraduate degree or a PhD from a listed UKVI majority English-speaking country, completed within 5 years; India is not on the list. Exemptions are assessed case by case.
english_waiver.quote: English Language competency exemptions will be assessed on a case-by-case basis in line with the below guidance. | Applicants who have successfully completed an undergraduate degree (of at least three years duration), a postgraduate taught degree (of at least one year), or a PhD in one of the following UKVI-defined majority English speaking countries are not usually required to complete an additional English language test.

supervisor.value: The University's PhD application steps say you must get written confirmation that a supervisor has agreed before you apply. Physics describes two routes (apply to a listed funded or non-funded project, or approach a supervisor with a speculative proposal) and asks you to name your intended supervisor, but its application procedure says to name potential supervisors only 'if possible'.
supervisor.quote: You must receive written confirmation that your supervisor(s) have agreed to submit you before progressing with your application.

also.quote: There two ways to apply. You can search our list of funded or non-funded projects or, you can approach a supervisor and present a speculative research proposal. | Ideally, you should indicate the research group and, if possible, names of potential supervisors.

funding.value: All scholarships, bursaries and awards are competitive. Funded projects come from EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Award and STFC studentships, other funders and research grants. Self-funded students get a research and training support grant.
funding.quote: All scholarships, bursaries or other awards are offered on a competitive basis. | The Department offers a range of funded PhD projects through a variety of funders, and research grants

entry_route.value: A first or upper-second-class (2:1) degree in physics or a related subject, plus strong motivation for research
entry_route.quote: Applicants should hold, or expect to gain, a first or upper second class degree in physics or a relevant related subject, and be exceptionally motivated for research.

notes: Successful applicants whose nationality is not exempt need an ATAS certificate, which takes time, so the College advises applying early. Applications go through King's Apply under 'Physics Research MPhil/PhD (full-time) programme'; decisions are aimed within eight weeks.
